title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 85 (Company's register of charges)

content.overview: Every company must keep at its registered office a prescribed register of charges containing the particulars required for charges and floating charges affecting its property, assets or undertakings, together with copies of the instruments creating the charges. The register and instruments are open to inspection during business hours by Members and creditors without fee, and by other persons on payment of prescribed fees, subject to reasonable restrictions in the articles.

content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 85 (Company's register of charges). Every company must keep at its registered office a register of charges in the prescribed form and manner, including prescribed particulars of charges and floating charges affecting company property, assets or undertakings. A copy of the instrument creating each charge must also be kept at the registered office with the register. The register and instruments are open for inspection during business hours by any Member or creditor without payment of fees, and by any other person on payment of prescribed fees, subject to reasonable restrictions the company may impose by its articles. Failure to comply with the charge-registration chapter may engage the current penalties in section 86. Legal verification remains open.

sections.heading: Register and required particulars
sections.body: Every company must keep at its registered office a register of charges in the prescribed form and manner, containing the prescribed particulars of charges and floating charges affecting any property or assets of the company or any of its undertakings.

sections.heading: Instrument copies
sections.body: A copy of the instrument creating the charge must be kept at the registered office with the register of charges.

sections.heading: Inspection rights
sections.body: The register and instruments are open to inspection during business hours by any Member or creditor without fee, or by any other person on payment of prescribed fees, subject to reasonable restrictions imposed by the company's articles.

hypotheticals.question: A creditor seeks to inspect the company's register of charges and the instruments creating charges. What does section 85 provide?
hypotheticals.analysis: The register and instruments are open for inspection during business hours. A Member or creditor may inspect without fee; any other person pays prescribed fees. Reasonable restrictions in the company's articles may apply.

hypotheticals.question: A company records a charge in its register but does not keep a copy of the instrument at the registered office. What section 85 requirement is implicated?
hypotheticals.analysis: Section 85 requires a copy of the instrument creating the charge to be kept at the registered office with the register of charges.

distinctions.title: Internal register and Registrar filing
distinctions.left: Section 85 requires the company to keep its own register of charges and copies of instruments at the registered office.
distinctions.right: Section 77 governs registration of charges with the Registrar.

misconceptions.trap: Treating the register as sufficient without retaining copies of the charge instruments.
misconceptions.correction: Section 85 also requires copies of instruments creating charges to be kept at the registered office.

misconceptions.trap: Assuming all members of the public can inspect the register for free.
misconceptions.correction: Members and creditors inspect without fee; other persons pay prescribed fees, subject to reasonable restrictions in the articles.

misconceptions.trap: Confusing the register-maintenance duty in section 85 with the filing/registration duties in section 77.
misconceptions.correction: Section 85 governs the company's register and inspection; section 77 covers registration of charges with the Registrar.
